question: Which iron and steel plant was established near the confluence of the rivers Subarnarekha and Kharkai?

options.text: Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited
Indian Iron and Steel Company Limited

solution:
The correct answer is __**Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Jamshedpur Steel Plant/**Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited**:

 
 
• Located in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand. 
 
• **This steel plant** has a strategic location at the **confluence of the Subarnarekha River and Kharkai River**.
 
• It is also known as Tata Steel which is a subsidiary of the Tata Group. 
 
• It was set up in 1907 by Jamsetji Tata.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• The Bhilai Steel Plant was established in 1955 with the help of the USSR.
 
• Durgapur Steel Plant is one of the integrated steel plants of Steel Authority of India Limited, located in Durgapur, West Bengal.
 
 
• It was set up with the help of the United Kingdom.
 
 
 
• Rourkela Steel Plant (RSP), the first integrated steel plant in the public sector in India, was set up with German collaboration with an installed capacity of 1 million tonnes.
 
• Bokaro Steel plant is located in Bokaro, Jharkhand and was the fourth public sector plant which was established in 1964 with the help of Russia.
 
• **Subarnarekha River**​​
 
 
• The Subarnarekha River, also recognized as the Swarnarekha River, flows through the Indian states of **Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha**.
 
• It is a** rain-fed river** sustaining millions of people residing in the areas it traverses.
 
• The river has its **origin near the village of Nagri**, located close to the city of Ranchi in the state of Jharkhand.
 
• One of the** notable features of the Subarnarekha River** is the **Hundru Waterfall**, where the river takes a plunge down a** 74m high cliff**.
 
• An interesting fact about its name: "**Subarnarekha**" translates to "**streak of gold**". This name is believed to come from the tradition of gold panning that was allegedly practiced near the origin of the river, specifically at a village named Piska.
 
• The river ultimately** flows into the Bay of Bengal **near the town of** Kirtania in Odisha**.
